findings.summary: runSync throws bare Error for 'Config file not found' while all other config-level validation uses ValidationError
evidence: src/cli/sync-command.ts:538: throw new Error(`Config file not found: ${configPath}`);
src/config/loader.ts:26-28: throw new ValidationError(`Failed to parse YAML config at ${filePath}: ${message}`);
src/cli/sync-command.ts:598: throw new Error('One or more repositories had errors during sync');
findings.suggestion: Use ValidationError for config-file-not-found (it is a user input error and should be classified as permanent by retry logic). The aggregation error at line 598 is arguably a different concern but could also benefit from a distinct error type.

findings.summary: Manifest parsing uses warn for parse failures while similar patterns elsewhere use debug
evidence: Contrast with safeCleanup in type-guards.ts which uses debug: log.debug(`Cleanup: ${label}: ${toErrorMessage(error)}`);
findings.suggestion: A corrupt manifest is recoverable (treated as 'no manifest'). Using warn is arguably correct since it signals data loss, but the pattern differs from the debug-level used in other swallowed-error scenarios. Consider standardizing: warn for data that may indicate user action needed, debug for purely internal recovery.

findings.summary: Label rename collision detection throws bare Error instead of ValidationError for user config problems
evidence: src/settings/labels/diff.ts:57-59: throw new Error(`Rename collision: both '${renameTargets.get(targetLower)}' and '${name}' rename to '${label.new_name}'`);
src/settings/labels/diff.ts:102-105: throw new Error(`Rename collision: '${name}' would rename to '${label.new_name}', but that label already exists`);
findings.suggestion: These are config validation errors (user misconfigured label renames). Use ValidationError for consistency with config-layer error classification. This also affects retry behavior — rename collisions should be treated as permanent errors without relying on message-pattern matching.

findings.summary: validateBranchName and validateSafeBranchName throw bare Error for input validation
evidence: src/vcs/branch-utils.ts:16: throw new Error('Branch name cannot be empty');
src/vcs/branch-utils.ts:20: throw new Error('Branch name cannot start with "." or "-"');
src/vcs/graphql-commit-strategy.ts:41-46: throw new Error(`Invalid branch name for GraphQL commit strategy: "${branchName}"...`);
findings.suggestion: These are input validation errors. Using ValidationError would allow retry logic to classify them as permanent without message-parsing, consistent with config validation.

findings.summary: checkExistingPR in all 3 strategies returns null for non-permanent errors, silently swallowing transient failures
evidence: src/vcs/github-pr-strategy.ts:58-69: catch(error) { if (isPermanentError(error)) { throw error; } ... return null; }
src/vcs/azure-pr-strategy.ts:55-66: catch(error) { if (isPermanentError(error)) { throw error; } ... return null; }
src/vcs/gitlab-pr-strategy.ts:113-124: catch(error) { if (isPermanentError(error)) { throw error; } ... return null; }
findings.suggestion: This is consistent across all 3 strategies (which is good). However, swallowing transient errors means a temporary network issue during PR check causes a duplicate PR to be created instead of retrying. The behavior is intentional for resilience but the debug-level logging means operators may not notice repeated duplicates. This is a design tradeoff rather than a bug.

findings.summary: GitHubAppTokenManager uses fetch API with manual HTTP status checking, producing differently formatted errors from the rest of the codebase
evidence: Compare with gh-api-utils.ts which uses gh CLI, producing errors like 'Command failed: gh api ...' with stderr
findings.suggestion: The token manager is the only module using fetch() directly for GitHub API calls. Its error messages use a different format ('GitHub API error: NNN') than the CLI-based errors elsewhere. This means the retry pattern matching in isPermanentError works differently for these errors (e.g., /401\b/ will match 'GitHub API error: 401' but the error structure lacks stderr). The inconsistency is minor since token manager errors are caught at a higher level, but consider standardizing the error format.
